**STEP 1 - Scene:** A small serving of cooked potato pieces on a white square plate, photographed from above at a near-top-down angle. It looks like the leftovers of a side dish.

**STEP 2 - Ruler:** The square plate's edges measure about 22 cm across. Area ≈ 22 × 22 ≈ 480 cm².

**STEP 3 - Items:** About 9–10 roasted or pan-fried potato chunks with golden-brown crusts. There is a faint orange smear on the plate, probably a trace of oil or seasoning, but it is too small to weigh separately.

**STEP 4 - Area:** The potato pieces cover about 17% of the plate, roughly 80 cm².

**STEP 5 - Volume:** The pieces are about 2–2.5 cm cubes piled up to about 1.5–1.6 cm on average. Gross volume ≈ 80 cm² × 1.6 cm ≈ 130 ml.

**STEP 6 - Grams:** Cut and roasted vegetable pieces have a bulk density of about 0.6–0.7 g/ml. 130 ml × 0.65 ≈ 85 g. Counting pieces individually (about 8 g each) gives about 75 g, so I use 75 g.

**STEP 7 - Energy:** Roasted or pan-fried potato is about 140 kcal per 100 g. 75 g × 1.4 ≈ 105 kcal.

**STEP 8 - Sanity check:** Roughly 75 g of potato across about 10 pieces is plausible for a small leftover portion. It is well below a full dinner-plate serving, which fits what is visible.
